explain.say: Mornings can feel busy, with lots to remember. Here is a trick. Look at the board. This is a morning checklist. It shows each job, one at a time, in order. You do not have to remember them all. The list remembers for you.

faq.a: A checklist holds the steps for you, so your brain does not have to. You just look, do one job and tick it.
asks: Why do I need a list?
Tell me about Wake and wash

faq.q: What if I forget a step?
faq.a: That is okay. Look back at your list and find the first box with no tick. Do that one next.

faq.q: How do I make my own checklist?
faq.a: Draw a small picture for each morning job. Put them in order from top to bottom. A grown-up you trust can help you stick it up where you can see it.
asks: Can I make my own list?

faq.q: What if my morning is different one day?
faq.a: Some days change, like a holiday or a trip. A grown-up can help you change the pictures on your list. Then you still know what comes next.

faq.q: How long should my morning take?
faq.a: Every family is different. You can ask a grown-up what time you need to be ready, and put a clock picture at the end of your list.

facts: A visual checklist uses pictures, so you can follow it even before you read well.
Dentists usually suggest brushing your teeth for about two minutes.

quiz.say: You finished breakfast. How do you know what to do next?
quiz.show: How do you know the next job?
quiz.why: The checklist shows the next box with no tick. It tells you what comes next.

wrong.1: Guessing can mix you up. The list knows the order.
wrong.2: You do not need to wait. Your list can tell you.

quiz.say: What do you do when a job is done?
quiz.show: What do you do when a job is done?
quiz.why: A tick shows the job is done, so you can move on to the next one.

wrong.1: No need to start again. Just move to the next box.
wrong.2: Keep your list. You can use it again tomorrow.
